title: Texas Live Oak: Ancient Texas Live Oaks You Can Visit
meta_description: A tougher inland live oak built for Hill Country droughts. Austin's Treaty Oak, about 500 years old, survived a 1989 poisoning.
intro: Texas Live Oak is the tougher inland cousin of the coastal live oak, built to survive Hill Country droughts and freezes that would kill its Gulf Coast relative. The old ones carry more history than botanical fame. Austin's Treaty Oak, reckoned at about 500 years old and known locally as the father of the forest, survived a 1989 poisoning that killed two thirds of it, then set acorns again eight years later. The Battle Oaks nearly fell in 1923 to make room for a university building, until a classics professor talked the committee out of it. In 1872 a priest is said to have chosen the site of St. Edward's University by standing under the Sorin Oak, already about a century old. Fort Worth's Turner Oak kept a farmer's gold buried in its roots through the Civil War, dug up afterward to help pay off the young town's debts.
